insights.title: Market trend — YCP is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-30.0%, now 9.0%).
insights.body: In YCP, 9.0% of installs now turn into new subs — -30.0% versus last period. It is about 40% of revenue (a big revenue market): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue +5.6% does not match new subs -2.8% from 7 days earlier — this growth is not coming from new customers.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 10-03 vs 09-26 is +5.6%, but App Total New Subs on 09-26 vs 09-19 was -2.8% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YMK is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-4.0% vs Install +6.9%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YMK New Subs -4.0% vs Install +6.9% (worse than its installs); YCP New Subs -30.4% vs Install +1.9% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total New Subs (-4.5% vs -14.8%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total New Subs in US is -4.5% while all countries together are -14.8% — a gap of +10.3pp. US is about 42% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install +5.4% — Paid Install is behind most of it (+1,278, +9.2%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 33,381, against 31,678 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +1,703. Where that came from: Paid Install +1,278 (+9.2%), SEO Install +651 (+36.8%), Organic Install -81 (-0.5%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (+1,278, +9.2%) and is now 45.2% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting toward SEO Install (+36.8% vs +5.4% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 2,420, +36.8% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved +5.4% — a difference of +31.4 percentage points. SEO Install is now 7.2% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.
